newsitem.title: CHINA: China unlikely to cut bank interest rates soon.
newsitem.headline: China unlikely to cut bank interest rates soon.

text.p: China is unlikely to reduce bank interest rates again in the short term following the two cuts in May and August last year, the China Securities newspaper said on Monday.
The official newspaper said last year's cuts had achieved the aims of easing the interest burden on state firms, cutting costs for banks and increasing the rate of currency circulation.

China's average bank deposit interest rates fell 2.48 percentage points as a result of the two cuts in 1996. The newspaper said this was the maximum possible given the inflation rate and the impact already apparent on bank deposits.
China's current annual bank deposit interest rate is a little more than one percentage point over the inflation rate, which prevents the central bank from cutting rates again, the newspaper said.
China has cut bank interest rates five times since 1979, each time at a point where the deposit rate was at least two percentage points higher than the inflation rate, the newspaper said.
"In the immediate future the possibility of an interest rate cut is not great," the newspaper said, but added:
"Of course, it is not possible to rule out the possibility of the government taking special measures based on the overall balance of factors in the development of the national economy."
